newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still mixed, range bound late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still mixed, range bound late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained narrowly mixed late Friday in light activity, with reports of slightly firmer physical values supporting the front of the board though prices remained in the recent range.
At 1415 EDT, August inched up 0.2 cent to $2.125 per million British thermal units, while September was one-half cent higher at $2.115. Others were still narrowly mixed.

"I don't see us running significantly in either direction. I think there's a lot of swing gas to be bought after the July fourth weekend, but if we get another big (AGA) inventory build, it could be bearish," said one East Coast trader.

With hot weather expected to return to the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic over the weekend and last into next week and above-normal temperatures forecast for the Midwest, most expected July prices to be fairly well supported when flows begin next week.
But they said demand typically slows in early July during the Independence Day holiday and some industrial shut downs.

Chart traders noted August was still clinging to support along the up trendline at $2.105, with more buying expected at the recent $2.08 low. Trendline resistance was seen at $2.27, with further selling likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.
Some technicians said weekly stochastics were close to crossing to the downside.

In the July cash Friday, Gulf Coast gas firmed slightly to the low-to-mid teens. July Midcon pipes were steady to down slightly at about $2. New York city gate gas for July was quoted in the mid-$2.40s, up five cents on the day.
NYMEX said 19,238 contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
On the KCBT, August gained one cent to $2.01, while deferreds were steady to 1.5 cents lower. The August East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 11.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
